shots.text: Reaching orbit takes speed as well as height. What if some of the machinery that gives a payload that speed could stay in space?

sentences.text: Reaching orbit takes speed as well as height.
What if some of the machinery that gives a payload that speed could stay in space?

shots.text: A skyhook is a rotating tether in orbit. Near the bottom of its swing, its tip moves against the orbital motion, reducing the speed an approaching payload needs to match.

sentences.text: A skyhook is a rotating tether in orbit.
Near the bottom of its swing, its tip moves against the orbital motion, reducing the speed an approaching payload needs to match.

shots.text: A launch vehicle climbs to the meeting point. Position, speed and timing must align. A grapple secures the payload, and the tether carries the load.

sentences.text: A launch vehicle climbs to the meeting point.
Position, speed and timing must align.
A grapple secures the payload, and the tether carries the load.

shots.text: As the tether turns, the payload gains orbital energy.

sentences.text: As the tether turns, the payload gains orbital energy.

shots.text: At a chosen release point, it leaves on its own trajectory.

sentences.text: At a chosen release point, it leaves on its own trajectory.

shots.text: That energy comes from the tether's motion. Before the next handoff, the system must recover. Propulsion, or carefully planned returning cargo, could help restore what the outgoing payload took.

sentences.text: That energy comes from the tether's motion.

shots.text: One tether could become part of a transport network: a lunar lunavator, an anchor at Phobos, and routes further into the solar system.

shots.text: Skyhook Industries explores that possibility. Design and test a flight in Flight Studio. Build and supply a network in Expeditions. Start with one handoff. See where it could lead.
